newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber futures end sharply lower to limit.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber futures end sharply lower to limit.

text.p: CME lumber futures ended sharply lower to down the daily limit of $10.00 per thousand board feet in January with limitless November pacing the setback on long liquidation, traders said.
January fell the limit to $397.40 per tbf and limitless November ended $17.70 lower at $463.70 after falling as much as $26.40 earlier in the session. Other months ended $9.30 to $4.00 lower.
Long liquidation, partly sparked by an easier undertone to the cash market, weighed on futures. Buyers were sparse and buying mostly consisted of short covering, traders said.

"The cash (market) has definitely slowed down. A lot of the rally 10 days ago was emotional after the mill by mill quotas were announced and a number of my cash (sources) are looking for a $40 to $50 correction in the cash market before there is buying interest again," said Curt Cunningham, President of Pacific Futures Trading.

Cash sources are looking for spruce prices to retrace back to the last legitimate active trading in the cash. Cash prices shot up after the mill quotas were announced in Canada and demand for cash has since subsided, Cunningham added.
Liquidation in November came ahead of Friday's expiration.
"It looks like weak longs are getting out of the market," one trader said.
ING notably sold November and selling was scattered in active January despite its very large discount to the cash market. Janauary was down to its lowest price level since November 1, traders added.
